1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5.name: English Opening: Anglo-Grünfeld Defence
1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5.background: This independent line of the English Opening generally parallels the development of its 1.d4 counterpart, the Grünfeld Defence, well into the game, hence its name. Ernst Grünfeld introduced that defence into international play at the Bad Pistyan tournament in April 1922.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.cxd5.strategy: Settles the centre at once: White trades the c-pawn for Black's central pawn and, after the recapture, can attack the knight on d5 with the c3-knight. The simplest way to a normal game, with the initiative in White's hands.

1.c4 Nf6 2.Nc3 d5 3.cxd5 Nxd5.strategy: The natural recapture: the knight reaches the centre, develops and attacks the knight on c3. Black enjoys central space and easy development, but the knight is exposed and White can start working against it at once.
